CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL JUDGMENT

The complainant/respondent in Crl.A.No.83/2012 on the file of the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Davanagere (for short 'the First Appellate Court') is impugning the judgment dated 03.03.2014 acquitting accused No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code (for short 'the IPC) and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act (for short 'the DP Act') by setting aside the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 30.06.2012 passed in CC No.290/2007 on the file of learned JMFC, Honnali (for short 'the Trial Court').
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their rank and status before the Trial Court.

Brief facts of the case are that, the complainant filed the first information against accused Nos.1 to 3 alleging commission of offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of DP act.

It is the specific contention of the complainant that she had married accused No.1 on 04.07.2002 and at the time of marriage, the accused have demanded dowry of Rs.1,20,000/- out of which, they have received Rs.1,14,000/- on various dates.
It is her further contention that after marriage, she was ill-treated by the accused by demanding additional dowry.
It is the specific contention of the complainant that on 13th and 14th of February, 2007, accused No.1 assaulted her all over the body, caused injuries and treated her with cruelty.
There by it is stated that accused Nos.1 to 3 have committed offence as stated above.

sentences.text: On the basis of statement of the complainant recorded, while she was taking treatment at McGann Hospital, Shivamogga, the FIR came to be registered against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the above stated offences and after investigation, the charge sheet came to be filed.
The complainant examined herself as PW1 and got examined PWs.2 to 20 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 15 and identified MO1 in NC: 2024:KHC:32495 support of her contention.
The accused have denied all the incriminating materials available on record and got examined DWs.1 to 5 and got marked Exs.D.1 to 11 in support of their contention.

The trial Court after taking into consideration all these materials on record, came to the conclusion that the prosecution is successful in proving the guilt of accused No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC and sentenced him to undergo simple imprisonment for 3 years and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- and in default to undergo SI for 1 month and he was also convicted for the offence punishable under Section 3 of DP Act and was sentenced to undergo SI for 5 years and to pay fine of Rs.1,14,000/- and in default to undergo SI for 3 months.
He was convicted for the offence punishable under Section 4 of DP Act and sentenced to undergo SI for 1 year and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- and in default, to undergo SI for 1 month.
It is also ordered that out of fine amount collected by accused No.1, a sum of Rs.1,14,000/- to be paid to PW1 as compensation.
However, the trial Court acquitted accused Nos.2 and 3 for the above said offences.
Being aggrieved by the same, accused No.1 challenged his conviction before the first Appellate Court in Crl.A.No.83/2012.

NC: 2024:KHC:32495 The first appellate Court on re-appreciation of materials on record came to the conclusion that the prosecution is not successful in proving the guilt of the accused and accordingly, allowed the appeal, set-aside the impugned judgment of conviction, convicting the accused No.1.
Being aggrieved by the same, the complainant is before this Court.
5. Heard Sri.B.S.Prasad, learned counsel for the appellant and Smt.N.Anitha Girish, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1-State.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 is absent and his arguments is taken as nil.
Perused the materials including the trial Court records.

6. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the impugned judgment of acquittal passed by the First Appellate Court suffers from perversity or illegality and calls for interference by this court? "
NC: 2024

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 7.
It is the specific contention of the prosecution that PW1 being complainant married accused No.1 on 04.07.2002 and this fact contention is not in dispute.

It is the contention of the prosecution that accused No.1 had demanded dowry of Rs.1,20,000/- at the time of marriage and out of the same,
Rs.1,14,000/- was paid by the complainant and her parents.
To prove this contention, the complainant examined herself as PW1, her father as PW4, brother as PW5, an independent witnesses PW9 and PW13 and her mother as PW10.

All these witnesses consistently stated about the A L Kalpana @ Latha vs The State Of Karnataka By Nymathi Police ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81272686/
3 demand made by accused No.1 for dowry and receiving an amount of Rs.1,14,000/- on various dates, as stated by them.

sentences.text: Even though, these witnesses were cross examined at length, nothing has been elicited to disbelieve their version.
Evidence of these prosecution witnesses are consistent with regard to material particulars.
Minor inconsistencies in the evidence is liable to be ignored as they do not go to the root of the matter.
NC: 2024:KHC:32495 There is absolutely no reason as to disbelieve the version of the independent witnesses who supported the case of the prosecution.
It is pertinent to note PWs.11 and 12 have also spoken about the demand for dowry and PW12 is the relative of the accused.
Even though accused No.1 had stepped into the witness box and deposed as DW1, the version of prosecution regarding demand and acceptance of dowry remain unshaken.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the prosecution is successful in proving the guilt of accused No.1 for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act who is liable for conviction.
8. Second contention taken by the prosecution is with regard to treating of PW1 with cruelty.
PW1 has stepped into the witness box and deposed regarding ill-treatment meted by accused in general and by accused No.1 in particular.
She states about the incident that had taken place on 13.02.2007 and 14.02.2007 and narrated in detail about the physical torture meted to her.
Her contention was also reiterated by her father, mother and brother and also the other witnesses.
It is pertinent to note that the statement of PW1 was recorded while she was admitted in McGann Hospital, on 15.02.2007.

The Doctor, who examined PW1 has issued the wound certificate as NC:
2024:KHC:32495 per Ex.P11, which discloses that she had sustained as many as 7 injuries, which are all simple in nature.

However, the wound certificates fully corroborates the contention of PW1 that she was physically assaulted and tortured by accused No.1.
9.
The author of Ex.P.11 i.e., the Doctor working in McGann Hospital was examined as PW17.
Even though the learned counsel for the accused cross-examined the witness at length, nothing has been elicited from him to disbelieve his version.
As per Ex.P.11 issued by PW17, the history of injury as stated by the injured is that the incident had occurred from 08.02.2007 up to a week and the injured was examined on 15.02.2007 at 5.00 p.m.
It is the specific contention of PW1 that she was assaulted by accused No.1 on 13.02.2007 and 14.02.2007, which is probabalised by Ex.P.11 and evidence of PW17.
PW1 and other prosecution witnesses also spoke about the cruelty meted to PW1 on many other occasions.

There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the version of the injured PW1 and PW17-the doctor who treated her on 15.02.2007.
10.
It is pertinent to note that Ex.P.15 is the copy of the birth certificate of child on 14.09.2010 and father being NC: 2024:KHC:32495 G.Raghavendra, who is accused No.1 and mother being one Shanta.
PW1 categorically stated that accused No.1 had married one Shanta and it is his second marriage and had begotten children.
Ex.P.15 substantiates her contention in that regard.

There is absolutely no explanation with regard to this document by accused No.1.
11.

The cumulative effect of these facts and circumstances necessarily go to show that prosecution is successful in proving the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC as well.

Therefore, accused is liable to be convicted for the offence both under IPC as well as under A L Kalpana @ Latha vs The State Of Karnataka By Nymathi Police ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81272686/
4 DP Act.

sentences.text:
12. I have gone through the judgment of conviction passed by the trial Court, it has taken into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before it and had arrived at a right conclusion in convicting accused No.1, holding that the prosecution successful in proving the guilt of the accused No.1 and in acquitting other accused.
13.
I have also gone through impugned judgment of acquittal passed by the First Appellate Court.

Even though the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:32495 First Appellate Court referred to evidence of various witnesses, it has given flimsy reasons to disbelieve the version of the prosecution which cannot be sustained when there are strong materials such as wound certificate, birth certificate of the child, said to have born to accused No.1 through his second marriage, which is coupled with evidence of the injured-PW1 and corroborated by the other prosecution witnesses.
I do not find any justification for First Appellate Court to ignore the clinching materials for the purpose of acquitting the accused.
The First Appellate Court has given unreasonable weightage to the minor inconsistencies, which resulted in grave injustice.

14. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that even though learned Magistrate has passed an order for grant of maintenance, accused No.1 is successfully denying the payment of maintenance amount and there by the complainant and her daughter are virtually in hard situation and they are at mercy of others.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case in the light of the matter is placed on record, the conduct of accused No.1 appears to be not acceptable and is liable for conviction.

Hence, I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment of acquittal passed by the First Appellate Court is - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:32495 liable to be set aside and the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Trial Court is liable to be restored.

Accordingly, I proceed to answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Appeal is allowed.
(ii) The impugned judgment dated 03.03.2014 passed in Crl.A.No.83/2012 on the file of the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Davanagere acquitting respondent No.2 is set aside.
